blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Scene Graph Anticipation (SGA) predicts object relationships in future video frames. Continuous-time SGA models evolve each subject-object pair with an independent Neural ODE, so relationships sharing an entity cannot influence one another during integration, and nothing prevents mutually exclusive predictions, such as "sitting on" and "standing on", for the same pair. We introduce CoupledSGA, which links such relationships through a Relationship Interaction Graph with graph attention inside the ODE vector field, and adds a Structural Consistency Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{SC}$) based on a matrix of mutually exclusive predicates.
  Developing CoupledSGA revealed a limitation of the evaluation protocol. With-Constraint evaluation keeps one predicate per group for each subject-object pair, so its R@K and mR@K cannot capture the within-group violations targeted by $\mathcal{L}_{SC}$: we prove they are unchanged whenever each group's winning predicate and its score are held fixed. We further show that the gradient of $\mathcal{L}_{SC}$ depends on predicate scores rather than ground-truth labels: for two-predicate rules it amplifies the ordering the model already holds, and when all scores in a group are equal it suppresses predicates in more exclusion rules more strongly, explaining why the penalty can lower recall while improving consistency.
  On Action Genome, activating $\mathcal{L}_{SC}$ after two warm-up epochs reduces R@20 from 42.21% to 35.18% while lowering the No-Constraint contradiction rate from 45.92% to 4.07% (matched-budget R@20: 40.48% CoupledSGA vs. 44.78% SceneSayerODE). CoupledSGA is a testbed, not a state-of-the-art claim: With-Constraint recall captures the cost of enforcing structural consistency but not the improvement. We recommend reporting No-Constraint results alongside a contradiction rate for methods that constrain predicate co-activation.

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 导言

blocks.en:
Scene Graph Anticipation (SGA) ( Peddi et al., 2024 ) aims to predict the
future relationships between entities in a video, representing them as ⟨ \langle subject, predicate, object ⟩ \rangle triplets. Its evaluation protocols
inherit established metrics from Scene Graph Generation
(SGG) ( Xu et al., 2017 ; Zellers et al., 2018 ) and Video Scene Graph Generation
(VidSGG) ( Cong et al., 2021 ; Feng et al., 2023 ) . In particular, Recall@ K K (R@ K K )
reduces the penalty associated with correct predictions that are not annotated in
the ground truth ( Xu et al., 2017 ) , while mean Recall@ K K (mR@ K K ) mitigates
the dominance of frequent predicate classes ( Chen et al., 2019 ) . These metrics
are commonly reported under two evaluation protocols: With Constraint, which
restricts the number of predicates that each subject–object pair can contribute
to the evaluation, and No Constraint, which permits multiple predicates per
pair ( Peddi et al., 2025 ; Peddi et al., 2024 ) . Although these protocols
provide complementary views of predictive performance, their ability to measure
structural consistency has received less attention.

blocks.en:
Structural consistency is important in applications that require reliable
predictions before an interaction occurs ( Furnari and Farinella, 2019 ; Gammulle et al., 2019 ) .
For example, a person cannot simultaneously be sitting on and standing on the same chair in the same relational context. Nevertheless, a
scene graph anticipation model may assign high scores to both predicates for the
same subject–object pair. For the Spatial and Contacting groups of Action
Genome ( Ji et al., 2020 ) , predicates are decoded using independent
sigmoid outputs. Consequently, mutually exclusive predicates are not necessarily
forced to compete, and the decoder can produce structurally inconsistent
predictions. Whether such inconsistencies affect the reported evaluation results
depends on the predictions retained by the evaluation protocol.

In the evaluation implementation released with SceneSayer ( Peddi et al., 2024 ) ,
the With-Constraint protocol retains the highest-scoring predicate from each
predicate group for a given subject–object pair, whereas the No-Constraint
protocol allows multiple predicates to be retained. As a result, With-Constraint
evaluation may discard evidence of a contradiction before the predictions are
scored. For example, sitting on and standing on both belong to the
Contacting group, so retaining only the highest-scoring predicate prevents both
from appearing in the evaluated output. Thus, a prediction may violate a structural
exclusion rule before filtering, yet the violation may remain invisible to the
reported recall metrics after filtering.

This issue emerged during the development of CoupledSGA, illustrated in
Figure 1 . CoupledSGA extends SceneSayerODE, the Neural Ordinary
Differential Equation (Neural ODE) variant of SceneSayer ( Peddi et al., 2024 ) ,
in which each subject–object pair is modelled by an independent Neural
ODE ( Chen et al., 2018 ) . Because the trajectories are integrated independently,
relationships that share an entity cannot directly influence one another during
temporal evolution. CoupledSGA introduces two complementary mechanisms. First, a
Relationship Interaction Graph (RIG) connects relationships that share an entity,
and graph attention ( Brody et al., 2022 ) within the ODE vector field enables
their representations to interact during integration. Second, a Structural
Consistency Loss ( ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} ) penalises the simultaneous activation of predicate
pairs specified as mutually exclusive in an exclusion matrix. The RIG facilitates
interaction between related relationships, whereas ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} explicitly
regularises predicate co-activation.

blocks.en:
The central finding of this work concerns the limitations of the evaluation
protocol rather than a claim of improved predictive performance. Every exclusion
rule considered in our matrix relates two predicates within the same predicate
group. Consequently, the With-Constraint protocol cannot retain both predicates
involved in any of these violations for the same subject–object pair. We formally
prove that, when the winning predicate and its score in each group remain fixed,
With-Constraint R@ K K and mR@ K K are unchanged regardless of whether a
within-group exclusion rule is violated (Proposition 5.1 ).
Therefore, these metrics alone cannot quantify the structural improvements
targeted by ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} . This result has an important implication: improvements in
structural consistency cannot be established solely through With-Constraint
recall.

Experiments on Action Genome are consistent with this analysis. Under a matched training budget, CoupledSGA achieves an R@20 of 40.48%, compared with
44.78% for SceneSayerODE. In a controlled comparison, activating ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} after two warm-up epochs reduces R@20 from 42.21% to 35.18%. Under the
No-Constraint protocol, the same change reduces the contradiction rate from
45.92% to 4.07%, while coupling alone reduces it from 54.40% to 45.92%. These
results are not intended to establish state-of-the-art performance. Rather, they
illustrate the trade-off between recall and structural consistency and show that
With-Constraint recall captures the cost of enforcing consistency without
reflecting the corresponding structural improvement.

blocks.en:
The findings motivate a more informative evaluation practice for SGA methods that
explicitly regularise predicate co-activation. In addition to standard
With-Constraint metrics, evaluations should report No-Constraint results and a
contradiction rate, defined as the proportion of (subject–object pair, predicate
group) instances in which the two highest-scoring predicates form an excluded pair.
Reporting these complementary measures would help distinguish predictive recall
from structural validity and provide a clearer assessment of the effects of
consistency constraints.

blocks.en: 2. Related Work
blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Static SGG extracted relationships from single images using message
passing ( Xu et al., 2017 ) and frequency priors ( Zellers et al., 2018 ) .
STTran ( Cong et al., 2021 ) added factorised spatial and temporal attention for
video, and DSG-DETR ( Feng et al., 2023 ) modelled long-term dependencies over object tracklets.
These models label frames they have observed, so their numbers are not a target
for anticipation. SceneSayer ( Peddi et al., 2024 ) introduced SGA and solved
it with per-pair Neural ODEs and Neural SDEs. Action
anticipation ( Furnari and Farinella, 2019 ; Gammulle et al., 2019 ) predicts coarse
labels rather than relational structure.

blocks.en:
Under With Constraint, R@ K K depends on the scores only through the within-group arg ⁡ max \arg\max and the ranking of kept triplets. By Corollaries 5.3 and 5.4 , ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} moves the arg ⁡ max \arg\max for reasons
unrelated to the label. Applied while the ordering is unreliable, it consolidates
whichever errors are present; applied once the ordering is largely correct, its
effect on the arg ⁡ max \arg\max is small. We therefore hypothesise that its contribution to With-Constraint recall is
non-positive early in training and near zero later; this does not follow from the
gradient alone, since recall also depends on the supervised terms.

We separate three things here. The intended role of ℒ SC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SC}} is to reduce co-activation mass. Its unintended
optimisation effect is to reinforce the current ordering and to penalise
high-degree predicates. Hypothesis 1 is a prediction about
recall, not a measurement: it says that enabling the penalty early should depress
With-Constraint recall relative to leaving it off. Section 6.3 measures the effect of enabling it after two warm-up epochs.

blocks.en: 8. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8. 结论

blocks.en:
We set out to remove independent relation trajectories from continuous-time Scene
Graph Anticipation, and built CoupledSGA: a graph over relationships, coupled into
the vector field of a Neural ODE, with a penalty on mutually exclusive predicates.
Building it exposed a problem with the measurement rather than the model.

建筑它暴露出一个问题 测量而不是模型。

blocks.en:
What we prove: under the With-Constraint emission rule, a scored output can never
contain both members of a within-group exclusion rule, so recall computed under that protocol cannot register those violations. What we derive: the gradient of a
quadratic exclusion penalty is label-free, it widens whichever ordering a
two-predicate rule already has, and it breaks ties against predicates that appear
in many rules. What we observe: on a matched 600/200 split, CoupledSGA reaches
40.48% R@20 against 44.78% for SceneSayerODE, and in a controlled comparison,
enabling the penalty after two warm-up epochs lowers R@20 from 42.21% to 35.18%.
The second, which isolates the penalty, has the sign the analysis predicts. Under No Constraint, the
same change lowers the contradiction rate from 45.92% to 4.07%, and coupling
alone lowers it from 54.40% to 45.92%. On this measure, the penalty reduces contradictions at a recall cost, and With-Constraint recall reports only the cost.
